payload.text:
Cloud | Document | Roadmap | Discord

📕 Table of Contents - 💡 [What is RAGFlow?](#-what-is-ragflow) - 🎮 [Get Started](#-get-started) - 📌 [Latest Updates](#-latest-updates) - 🌟 [Key Features](#-key-features) - 🔎 [System Architecture](#-system-architecture) - 🎬 [Self-Hosting](#-self-hosting) - 🔧 [Configurations](#-configurations) - 🔧 [Build a Docker image](#-build-a-docker-image) - 🔨 [Launch service from source for development](#-launch-service-from-source-for-development) - 📚 [Documentation](#-documentation) - 📜 [Roadmap](#-roadmap) - 🏄 [Community](#-community) - 🙌 [Contributing](#-contributing)
## 💡 What is RAGFlow? [RAGFlow](https://ragflow.io/) is a leading open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation ([RAG](https://ragflow.io/basics/what-is-rag)) engine that fuses cutting-edge RAG with Agent capabilities to create a superior context layer for LLMs. It offers a streamlined RAG workflow adaptable to enterprises of any scale. Powered by a converged [context engine](https://ragflow.io/basics/what-is-agent-context-engine) and pre-built agent templates, RAGFlow enables developers to transform complex data into high-fidelity, production-ready AI systems with exceptional efficiency and precision. ## 🎮 Get Started Try our cloud service at [https://cloud.ragflow.io](https://cloud.ragflow.io).
## 🔥 Latest Updates - 2026-04-24 Supports DeepSeek v4. - 2026-03-24 [RAGFlow Skill on OpenClaw](https://clawhub.ai/yingfeng/ragflow-skill) — Provides an official skill for accessing RAGFlow datasets via OpenClaw. - 2025-12-26 Supports 'Memory' for AI agent. - 2025-11-19 Supports Gemini 3 Pro. - 2025-11-12 Supports data synchronization from Confluence, S3, Notion, Discord, Google Drive. - 2025-10-23 Supports MinerU & Docling as document parsing methods. - 2025-10-15 Supports orchestrable ingestion pipeline. - 2025-08-08 Supports OpenAI's latest GPT-5 series models. - 2025-08-01 Supports agentic workflow and MCP. - 2025-05-23 Adds a Python/JavaScript code executor component to Agent. - 2025-05-05 Supports cross-language query. - 2025-03-19 Supports using a multi-modal model to make sense of images within PDF or DOCX files. ## 🎉 Stay Tuned ⭐️ Star our repository to stay up-to-date with exciting new features and improvements! Get instant notifications for new releases! 🌟
## 🌟 Key Features ### 🍭 **"Quality in, quality out"** - [Deep document understanding](./deepdoc/README.md)-based knowledge extraction from unstructured data with complicated formats. - Finds "needle in a data haystack" of literally unlimited tokens. ### 🍱 **Template-based chunking** - Intelligent and explainable. - Plenty of template options to choose from. ### 🌱 **Grounded citations with reduced hallucinations** - Visualization of text chunking to allow human intervention. - Quick view of the key references and traceable citations to support grounded answers. ### 🍔 **Compatibility with heterogeneous data sources** - Supports Word, slides, excel, txt, images, scanned copies, structured data, web pages, and more. ### 🛀 **Automated and effortless RAG workflow** - Streamlined RAG orchestration catered to both personal and large businesses. - Configurable LLMs as well as embedding models. - Multiple recall paired with fused re-ranking. - Intuitive APIs for seamless integration with business. ## 🔎 System Architecture
## 🎬 Self-Hosting ### 📝 Prerequisites - CPU >= 4 cores - RAM >= 16 GB - Disk >= 50 GB - Docker >= 24.0.0 & Docker Compose >= v2.26.1 - Python >= 3.13 - [gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/docs/user_guide/install/): Required only if you intend to use the code executor (sandbox) feature of RAGFlow. > [!TIP] > If you have not installed Docker on your local machine (Windows, Mac, or Linux), see [Install Docker Engine](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/). ### 🚀 Start up the server 1. Ensure `vm.max_map_count` >= 262144: > To check the value of `vm.max_map_count`: > > ```bash > $ sysctl vm.max_map_count > ``` > > Reset `vm.max_map_count` to a value at least 262144 if it is not. > > ```bash > # In this case, we set it to 262144: > $ sudo sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=262144 > ``` > > This change will be reset after a system reboot. To ensure your change remains permanent, add or update the > `vm.max_map_count` value in **/etc/sysctl.conf** accordingly: > > ```bash > vm.max_map_count=262144 > ``` > 2. Clone the repo: ```bash $ git clone https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow.git ``` 3. Start up the server using the pre-built Docker images: > [!CAUTION] > All Docker images are built for x86 platforms. We don't currently offer Docker images for ARM64. > If you are on an ARM64 platform, follow [this guide](https://ragflow.io/docs/dev/build_docker_image) to build a Docker image compatible with your system. > The command below downloads the `v0.25.6` edition of the RAGFlow Docker image. See the following table for descriptions of different RAGFlow editions. To download a RAGFlow edition different from `v0.25.6`, update the `RAGFLOW_IMAGE` variable accordingly in **docker/.env** before using `docker compose` to start the server. ```bash $ cd ragflow/docker # git checkout v0.25.6 # Optional: use a stable tag (see releases: https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/releases) # This step ensures the **entrypoint.sh** file in the code matches the Docker image version. # Use CPU for DeepDoc tasks: $ docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d # To use GPU to accelerate DeepDoc tasks: # sed -i '1i DEVICE=gpu' .env # docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d ``` > Note: Prior to `v0.22.0`, we provided both images with embedding models and slim images without embedding models. Details as follows: | RAGFlow image tag | Image size (GB) | Has embedding models? | Stable? | |-------------------|-----------------|-----------------------|----------------| | v0.21.1 | ≈9 | ✔️ | Stable release | | v0.21.1-slim | ≈2 | ❌ | Stable release | > Starting with `v0.22.0`, we ship only the slim edition and no longer append the **-slim** suffix to the image tag. 4. Check the server status after having the server up and running: ```bash $ docker logs -f docker-ragflow-cpu-1 ``` _The following output confirms a successful launch of the system:_ ```bash ____ ___ ______ ______ __ / __ \ / | / ____// ____// /____ _ __ / /_/ // /| | / / __ / /_ / // __ \| | /| / / / _, _// ___ |/ /_/ // __/ / // /_/ /| |/ |/ / /_/ |_|/_/ |_|\____//_/ /_/ \____/ |__/|__/ * Running on all addresses (0.0.0.0) ``` > If you skip this confirmation step and directly log in to RAGFlow, your browser may prompt a `network abnormal` > error because, at that moment, your RAGFlow may not be fully initialized. > 5. In your web browser, enter the IP address of your server and log in to RAGFlow. > With the default settings, you only need to enter `http://IP_OF_YOUR_MACHINE` (**sans** port number) as the default > HTTP serving port `80` can be omitted when using the default configurations. > 6. In [service_conf.yaml.template](./docker/service_conf.yaml.template), select the desired LLM factory in `user_default_llm` and update the `API_KEY` field with the corresponding API key. > See [llm_api_key_setup](https://ragflow.io/docs/dev/llm_api_key_setup) for more information. > _The show is on!_ ## 🔧 Configurations When it comes to system configurations, you will need to manage the following files: - [.env](./docker/.env): Keeps the fundamental setups for the system, such as `SVR_HTTP_PORT`, `MYSQL_PASSWORD`, and `MINIO_PASSWORD`. - [service_conf.yaml.template](./docker/service_conf.yaml.template): Configures the back-end services. The environment variables in this file will be automatically populated when the Docker container starts. Any environment variables set within the Docker container will be available for use, allowing you to customize service beh

payload.body:
@monsterdavidliu-ux  
Do you think it's a new feature or an existing bug?

payload.author: monsterdavidliu-ux
payload.body:
I'd classify this as an **existing bug**, not a new feature.

**Why bug:** For MCP-wrapped agents, looking up a file by `doc_id` effectively only exposed download behavior (or wrong `Content-Disposition`), so inline preview in the client didn't work as users expect from the rest of the document/attachment flows. That's the gap reported in #15398.

**What the PR does:** Restores the intended behavior — inline preview for previewable types via explicit preview routes/headers and `preview_url` in DocGenerator output — without changing legacy `/document/download/...` to inline (those stay attachment/download semantics).

The new `/agents/attachments/{id}/preview` endpoint is the minimal API surface to fix that bug; I wouldn't treat it as a separate feature request.

Happy to retitle or adjust labels if the team prefers `fix` vs `feat` for endpoint additions.

`553-556`: _💤 Low value_

**Redundant dataset listing in the tool description.**

The full `dataset_description` is already embedded in the `ragflow_retrieval` tool description (Line 494). Appending it again here duplicates the entire dataset list across two tool descriptions, inflating the advertised tool payload (and token usage) for clients. Since this tool already returns datasets at call time, consider a static description without the appended list.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the

In `@mcp/server/server.py` around lines 553 - 556, The tool definition for
types.Tool with name "ragflow_list_datasets" is appending dataset_description
redundantly (duplicate of the long list already present in the ragflow_retrieval
tool); remove the concatenation of dataset_description from the
ragflow_list_datasets description and replace it with a concise static sentence
(e.g., "Returns a list of accessible datasets with IDs, names and short
descriptions.") so the full dataset list remains only in the ragflow_retrieval
tool and you avoid inflating the tool payload.
```

---

`488-488`: _⚡ Quick win_

**`list_tools` now fails entirely if `/chats` errors.**

`list_chats` raises on any non-200/non-zero response, and this call happens during tool discovery. A transient `/chats` failure (or a backend without that endpoint) will now break the entire `list_tools` response, making even `ragflow_retrieval` and `ragflow_list_datasets` undiscoverable. Consider degrading gracefully so a chat-listing hiccup doesn't take down tool discovery.

payload.author: xugangqiang
Khaostica
payload.body:
Hi @xugangqiang, thanks for the quick look! Confirmed — the bug is real and this PR fixes it.

**Root cause.** `/api/v1/datasets/{id}/ingestions/summary` returns the counts nested under `status` with `*_count` keys, but the overview hook (`useFetchOverviewTotal`) read flat top-level fields (`downloaded`/`processing`/`finished`/`failed`/`cancelled`). Those keys don't exist on the response, so every card except "Total Files" rendered `0`.

**Reproduction with the exact payload from #15304:**

```js
// API response from /ingestions/summary
{ "data": { "doc_num": 2576, "status": {
  "cancel_count": 0, "done_count": 937, "fail_count": 18, "running_count": 767, "unstart_count": 854
}}}

// BEFORE (old hook, reads flat fields):
{ cancelled: 0, failed: 0, finished: 0, processing: 0, downloaded: 0 }   // ❌ all zero

// AFTER (mapOverviewTotal, this PR):
{ cancelled: 0, failed: 18, finished: 937, processing: 767, downloaded: 854 }   // ✅ correct
```

These mapped values feed straight into the StatCards (`downloads.success`, `processing.value/success/failed`), so the overview now shows the real counts instead of `0`.

**Unit tests** (`web/src/pages/dataset/dataset-overview/utils.test.ts`) covering the full mapping, undefined input, missing `status`, and partial `status`:

```
PASS src/pages/dataset/dataset-overview/utils.test.ts
  mapOverviewTotal
    √ maps nested status counts to the flat overview fields
    √ defaults every field to 0 when status is missing
    √ defaults every field to 0 when data is undefined
    √ fills only the counts present in a partial status

Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total
Tests:       4 passed, 4 total
```

The change keeps the backend contract untouched and only adjusts the frontend mapping. Happy to attach before/after UI screenshots from a full stack run if that's helpful for the merge.

`69-72`: _⚡ Quick win_ **Inconsistent error response pattern across handlers.** The conditional `data: nil` for `CodeExceptionError` is applied in `Register` and `Setting` (lines 441–447), but not in `Login` (line 136), `LoginByEmail` (line 212), `Logout` (line 369), or `ChangePassword` (line 495). If those methods can also return `CodeExceptionError`, clients will receive inconsistent response shapes. Consider one of these approaches for consistency: 1. **Apply the pattern uniformly**: Add the same conditional logic to all error handlers that might return `CodeExceptionError`. 2. **Use the standard helper**: Replace inline error responses with the `jsonError` helper (defined in `kb.go`, lines 53–60), which always uses `"data": nil`.
Option 2: Refactor to use the standard `jsonError` helper ```diff user, code, err := h.userService.Register(&req) if err != nil { - var data interface{} = false - if code == common.CodeExceptionError { - data = nil - } - c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{ - "code": code, - "message": err.Error(), - "data": data, - }) + jsonError(c, code, err.Error()) return } ``` You would also need to define `jsonError` in this file or import it from a shared location.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@internal/handler/user.go` around lines 69 - 72, Handlers Register and Setting set response "data" to nil on common.CodeExceptionError but Login, LoginByEmail, Logout and ChangePassword do not, causing inconsistent response shapes; update those handlers (Login, LoginByEmail, Logout, ChangePassword) to use the same pattern by replacing their inline error responses with the standard jsonError helper (or, if jsonError is not accessible, add the conditional var data interface{} = false / if code == common.CodeExceptionError { data = nil } and pass that into the response) so all error responses consistently return "data": nil for CodeExceptionError; ensure you import or define jsonError from kb.go if you choose that route. ```

payload.body: I think you file you are trying to change is a script (one off usage) - which means it's not part of the server side logic?

payload.author: jony376
payload.body:
Hi @xugangqiang, thanks for the review.

You’re right that tools/scripts/mysql_migration.py is an operational migration script, not runtime API code. The change is still intentional:

The script is run against real tenant data during upgrades (tenant_llm → tenant_model_provider). If llm_factory or tenant_id contains a single quote (or other special characters), the old f-string INSERT breaks with a SQL syntax error and can leave the migration half-applied.
#15312 reports that failure mode; parameterized placeholders fix it without changing server behavior.
This matches how other stages in the same file should be written (safe batch inserts), even for one-off tooling.
I’ve rebased/merged latest main and kept upstream’s current_ts * 1000 timestamp handling while preserving parameterized inserts.

Happy to close if maintainers prefer handling this only in docs/runbooks, but I believe the script fix is low risk and prevents a real migration failure for some tenants.

Thanks again.

payload.body: @Rene0422  May I know if you have conducted testing on your side? if so, please upload testing evidence. Also, is it possible to add unit test or end-2-end test?

payload.author: Rene0422
payload.body:
> @Rene0422 May I know if you have conducted testing on your side? if so, please upload testing evidence. Also, is it possible to add unit test or end-2-end test?

Hi @xugangqiang — the unit test is already in this PR at
`test/unit_test/api/apps/restful_apis/test_chat_completions_sanitize_floats.py`
(all 9 cases tagged `@pytest.mark.p1`).

It targets the **live source** of `_sanitize_json_floats` — extracted
from `chat_api.py` via the `ast` module and exec'd in an isolated
namespace exposing only stdlib `math`, so the test isn't a stale
copy and any future change to the sanitizer is exercised. Avoids
having to stub out the dozens of heavy imports `chat_api.py` pulls
in at module load (quart, peewee models, services, etc.).

Cases:

- `test_passthrough_for_healthy_values` — int / float / str / None /
  bool / list / dict pass through unchanged
- `test_nan_becomes_none` — top-level NaN → `None`
- `test_positive_and_negative_infinity_become_none` — parametrized
  over `inf` / `-inf`
- `test_nan_inside_dict_replaced` — sibling keys preserved verbatim
- `test_inf_inside_list_replaced` — surrounding elements preserved
- `test_deeply_nested_chunks_format` — the actual `reference.chunks`
  shape (list of dicts with `similarity` / `vector_similarity` /
  `term_similarity` scores, mixed NaN/Inf), which is the exact
  payload that triggered #15245
- `test_tuples_are_walked_and_returned_as_tuples` — container type
  preserved
- `test_numpy_float32_nan_caught_via_math_isnan` — `np.float64('nan')`,
  `np.float32('nan')`, `np.float16('nan')` all → `None`. Locks in the
  earlier review fix that swapped `isinstance(obj, float)` for a
  `math.isnan` probe so numpy scalar types are caught; uses
  `pytest.importorskip("numpy")` so CI doesn't gate on the optional
  dep
- `test_strings_are_not_treated_as_numeric` — `"NaN"` /
  `"Infinity"` stay as strings; verifies the `TypeError` swallow path

## Manual reproduction in dev

`POST /api/v1/chat/completions` with `stream=true` against a
dataset where retrieval scoring can yield `similarity=NaN` (small
dataset + a query whose tokens don't match well, so the cosine
denominator goes to zero).

**Before** the patch the SSE stream contains a frame like:

```
data:{"code": 500, "message": "failed to encode response: json:
unsupported value: NaN", "data": {"answer": "**ERROR**: ...",
"reference": []}}
```

**After** the patch the same stream completes cleanly with the
score serialized as `null` in `reference.chunks[*].similarity` /
`vector_similarity` / `term_similarity`, and the rest of the
payload is unchanged.

Happy to attach before/after captures (curl output + tee'd SSE log)
to the PR if useful — let me know.

**Actionable comments posted: 1**
🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
.github/workflows/tests.yml (1)
`204-211`: **TOCTOU window between probing and binding.** The probe selects a free block here, but the ports are not bound until `docker compose ... up -d` runs much later (Line 276). On a shared self-hosted runner a concurrent job can claim a probed port in that gap, so this reduces—but does not eliminate—collisions. MCP server discovery and listing is becoming a key infrastructure piece as the ecosystem grows. Having a standardized API to enumerate available servers makes it much easier for host applications to compose multi-step workflows.

In our work building [AI Workdeck](https://github.com/zeweihan/aiworkdeck) — an open-source workspace for document-heavy legal workflows — we rely on MCP servers as pluggable tools. A server list API like this would help us dynamically discover and connect to new document processing capabilities (OCR, NER, clause extraction, etc.) at runtime.

Quick question: are you planning to include metadata like tool schemas and capability tags in the listing response? That would enable automatic workflow composition — the host app could match incoming document types to the right server without manual configuration.

Nice contribution to the MCP tooling landscape!

@xugangqiang Thanks for the nudge — here's reproducible evidence beyond the unit test.

### Repro setup

- Local dev stack via `docker/docker-compose.yml`, frontend via `web/npm run dev` (Vite, StrictMode active — same code path as a genuine remount in production).
- Created a dataset, uploaded a small file, then clicked the parse ▶ on the document row (zero chunks, metadata disabled → the dialog mounts with `hidden=true` and the auto-fire `useEffect` runs on mount).
- Captured browser Network and the `ragflow-server` access log.

### Before — `main`

Each click produces **two** `POST /api/v1/documents/ingest` on distinct source ports within the same second:

[INFO] 172.20.0.1:41874 POST /api/v1/documents/ingest 1.1 200
[INFO] 172.20.0.1:41876 POST /api/v1/documents/ingest 1.1 200

Two success toasts also fired per click.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b1e03b2-9a8c-41d2-a40f-b6fa66722403



### After — this branch

The `autoFiredRef` latch prevents the second invocation. One toast, one POST per click:

[INFO] 172.20.0.1:36490 POST /api/v1/documents/ingest 1.1 200



https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b640b631-b5f3-4a99-b30c-e69d6031f398



The unit test in `reparse-dialog.test.tsx` codifies this guarantee so it doesn't regress.

payload.body:
> @nickmopen May I know the version/git commit for your testings? I can't re-produce with latest main.

@xugangqiang

Here's the recipe I used to reproduce it deterministically on `main`. The trigger is React 18 StrictMode's intentional double-invoke of the dialog's mount `useEffect` (active in `web/src/main.tsx`), so it shows up on the **Vite dev server**, not on a `vite build` production bundle.

Tested on `main` at `7f79b8486`'s parent (i.e. main without this PR). Repro:

1. `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d` (backend + deps, v0.25.6 image)
2. `cd web && npm run dev` — `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` if you run into OOM
3. Sign in, create a dataset, upload a small file (any 1-line `.txt` works)
4. Open DevTools → Network, filter `documents/ingest`, tick "Preserve log"
5. Click the ▶ icon on the row (state is `UNSTART`, `chunk_count=0`, `enable_metadata=false` — this puts the dialog into the `hidden=true` auto-fire path)

What I see: **two** identical `POST /api/v1/documents/ingest` per click, two "Operation succeeded" toasts. Backend access log from a single click (both lines within the same second, distinct source ports):

[INFO] 172.20.0.1:41874 POST /api/v1/documents/ingest 1.1 200
[INFO] 172.20.0.1:41876 POST /api/v1/documents/ingest 1.1 200

A couple of questions so we can match environments:
- Was your "can't reproduce" attempt against `npm run dev` or a built/served bundle?
- Was the document zero-chunk with metadata disabled (so the dialog mounts hidden)?
- Any console error / hot-reload skip that might have interfered with the StrictMode double-invoke?

Your original report said "**sometimes** the enqueue happens 2 times" in a v0.25 prod image — that intermittency suggests a same-instance re-fire of the same `useEffect` is the underlying mechanism, which the StrictMode case turns into a deterministic instance of the same path.

<!-- Answer -->
This PR looks correct. The fix addresses a classic React stale closure bug where `handleSave` closed over `metaData.values` (which only syncs on blur), so a Confirm click that races the blur would queue the pre-blur empty string `['']`. Reading from `tempValues` instead captures the real-time typed input regardless of whether blur has fired .

The dependency array update (adding `tempValues`) is also correct to keep the hook semantics sound, and the regression test properly validates the "Confirm without blur" path .

payload.author: dripsmvcp
payload.body:
Hey @Haruko386 👋 thanks for flagging this — honestly a fair thing to ask.

Let me be upfront: I didn't build this off my own DeerAPI key. I was filling a gap — DeerAPI is already a supported provider on the Python side (merged a while back in #10303, by the DeerAPI folks themselves), but the new Go API server didn't have a driver for it yet. So this PR just brings Go up to parity with what Python already does. I also called out in the description that I couldn't do a live end-to-end run from my environment and was leaning on CI + the shared OpenAI-compatible pattern the other drivers use.

On the "stopped registering" part — I poked at it just now, and the API itself still seems alive:

- `GET https://api.deerapi.com/v1/models` → `401` (just the normal "you forgot your key" response)
- `https://deerapi.com` → `301`

So the endpoint the driver talks to is still up. What you're describing sounds more like **they've closed new sign-ups**, which is different from the service being dead — and that part I genuinely can't confirm, so you may well be right.

I'll leave the call to you:

- **If new registration is really closed** → let's hold this one, and we should probably look at the Python provider too, since it'd be in the same spot.
- **If existing keys still work** (the API answering suggests they might) → merging keeps Go and Python consistent.

Either way I'm happy to follow your lead — close it, hold it, or tweak anything else. Just let me know 🙏

`4146-4148`: _⚡ Quick win_

**Clarify the behavior of `pass_all_history_messages` more precisely.**

The current description has several ambiguities:

1. "replace/use" is unclear - are these two different operations or synonyms?
2. It says "only the latest user message from the request" but doesn't clarify how this works when `question` is used instead of `messages`.
3. It doesn't explain what happens when `pass_all_history_messages=true` but only `question` is provided.

Consider revising to:

```markdown
- `"pass_all_history_messages"`: (*Body Parameter*), `boolean`
  Controls message history handling when both `chat_id` and `session_id` are provided. Defaults to `false`, meaning the server appends only the latest user message (from `messages` or `question`) to the stored session history. When `true`, the server replaces the stored session history with the full submitted `messages` array (or a single message if `question` is used).
```

This clarifies the append-vs-replace distinction and covers both `messages` and `question` input modes.

##### [What is the complete API flow for building a frontend UI with RAGFlow, covering dialogs, conversations, message history, streaming responses, and deletion?](https://app.dosu.dev/49f9a533-7254-4314-b3e9-a7313bc58cc8/documents/a4402f70-64e2-4eb0-b464-70bcbcc51355?utm_source=github&utm_medium=pr-comment&utm_campaign=docs-adoption&utm_content=page-update-link)

<details>
<summary>View Changes</summary>

````diff
@@ -173,15 +173,14 @@
 Content-Type: application/json
 ```
 
-> ⚠️ **Critical:** The frontend **must send the full conversation history** with every request. The backend is stateless during completion — it does NOT load previous messages from the database automatically.
-
-**Payload — First message:**
+> 💡 **Default behavior:** When `chat_id` and `session_id` are provided, you only need to send the **latest message**. The backend automatically loads stored conversation history from the database. To override this and send full conversation history instead, set `pass_all_history_messages: true`.
+
+**Payload — First message (default behavior):**
 ```json
 {
   "chat_id": "abc123def456",
   "session_id": "sess_new_002",
   "messages": [
-    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi! How can I help you?"},
     {"role": "user", "content": "What is RAGFlow?"}
   ],
   "stream": true,
@@ -191,11 +190,36 @@
 
 > **Note:** Either `session_id` or `conversation_id` can be used interchangeably to identify the session/conversation.
 
-**Payload — Second message (includes ALL previous history):**
+**Payload — Second message (default behavior):**
 ```json
 {
   "chat_id": "abc123def456",
   "session_id": "sess_new_002",
+  "messages": [
+    {"role": "user", "content": "How do I install it?"}
+  ],
+  "stream": true,
+  "quote": true
+}
+```
+
+**Alternative — Using `question` field:**
+```json
+{
+  "chat_id": "abc123def456",
+  "session_id": "sess_new_002",
+  "question": "How do I install it?",
+  "stream": true,
+  "quote": true
+}
+```
+
+**Optional — Send full conversation history:**
+```json
+{
+  "chat_id": "abc123def456",
+  "session_id": "sess_new_002",
+  "pass_all_history_messages": true,
   "messages": [
     {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi! How can I help you?"},
     {"role": "user", "content": "What is RAGFlow?"},
@@ -303,7 +327,7 @@
 ```
 
 **Key recommendations:**
-1. **Message state is local** — Load from API on session select, maintain locally during chat, send full array on each completion.
+1. **Message state is local** — Load from API on session select, maintain locally during chat, send only the latest message on each completion (unless using `pass_all_history_messages: true`).
 2. **Optimistic UI** — Append user message immediately before sending.
 3. **Streaming accumulation** — Replace the assistant placeholder content on each SSE event (it's accumulated, not delta).
 4. **Abort support** — Store an `AbortController` in state; call `controller.abort()` on navigation.
@@ -318,8 +342,8 @@
 1. GET /api/v1/chats → Load dialogs, select first (id: "dialog_A")
 2. GET /api/v1/chats/dialog_A/sessions → Load conversation list for sidebar
 3. POST /api/v1/chats/dialog_A/sessions  {"name": "New Chat"} → Create session (id: "sess_X")
-4. POST /api/v1/chat/completions  {chat_id, session_id, messages: [greeting, user_q1], stream:true} → SSE stream
+4. POST /api/v1/chat/completions  {chat_id, session_id, messages: [user_q1], stream:true} → SSE stream
 5. Stream ends → Backend auto-persists → Local state: [greeting, user_q1, assistant_a1]
-6. POST /api/v1/chat/completions  {messages: [greeting, user_q1, assistant_a1, user_q2], stream:true} → context-aware response
+6. POST /api/v1/chat/completions  {chat_id, session_id, messages: [user_q2], stream:true} → context-aware response (server loads history)
 7. User returns later → GET /api/v1/chats/dialog_A/sessions → session messages already persisted → resume chat
 ```

payload.body: `Document.id` is set directly from `drive_item.id`, but Graph only guarantees that ID is unique within a single drive. Since this connector scans multiple document libraries under the same site, that creates a cross-drive collision risk that can break deduplication and later update/delete flows. Please include `drive_id` in the document identifier or use a globally unique composite key.

<!-- Answer -->
Thanks for the PR! I reviewed how this SharePoint connector implementation aligns with RAGFlow's existing data source patterns. Here's a summary:

**Overall: The PR follows established patterns well across all areas.**

- **Backend connector** — correctly implements the `CheckpointedConnectorWithPermSync` interface with `load_credentials()`, `validate_connector_settings()`, `load_from_checkpoint()`, and `retrieve_all_slim_docs_perm_sync()` [[1]](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/blob/e6dd397531659db407d0823e18156bf8c818523a/common/data_source/sharepoint_connector.py). The MSAL token-callback approach for `GraphClient` is the right fix over the stub's raw-token string.

- **Sync integration** — `SharePoint._generate()` uses the `CheckpointOutputWrapper` pattern with proper tuple unpacking (`document, failure, next_checkpoint`), matching Confluence/Jira connectors [[2]](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/blob/e6dd397531659db407d0823e18156bf8c818523a/rag/svr/sync_data_source.py#L568-L581) [[3]](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/blob/e6dd397531659db407d0823e18156bf8c818523a/common/data_source/interfaces.py#L312-L354).

- **Frontend** — form fields (`site_url`, `tenant_id`, `client_id`, `client_secret`) follow the declarative `FormFieldConfig` pattern used by other connectors [[4]](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/blob/e6dd397531659db407d0823e18156bf8c818523a/web/src/components/dynamic-form.tsx#L62-L95), with localization in both `en.ts` and `zh.ts`.

- **Tests** — mock-based unit tests align with the existing test patterns for Dropbox and REST API connectors [[5]](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/blob/e6dd397531659db407d0823e18156bf8c818523a/test/unit_test/common/test_dropbox_connector.py) [[6]](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/blob/e6dd397531659db407d0823e18156bf8c818523a/test/unit_test/data_source/test_rest_api_connector.py).

**One minor note:** The best-effort ACL→`ExternalAccess` mapping is a reasonable pragmatic choice given the sync pipeline doesn't persist `ExternalAccess` yet — this is properly documented in the PR as a known limitation to extend later.

A few questions that might be worth considering:

1. How does the connector handle rate limiting / retry when traversing large document libraries with deeply nested folders?
2. Are there considerations for SharePoint-specific features like version history or archived sites?
3. What's the expected behavior if Azure AD credentials are rotated mid-sync?

payload.author: coderabbitai
payload.body:
[![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/15181?utm_source=github_walkthrough&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=change_stack)
📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough This PR secures OIDC ID-token verification by pinning signing algorithms at client initialization from provider metadata, filtered against a safe asymmetric allowlist, and validated during `jwt.decode` instead of trusting the unverified JWT header. It adds regression tests covering algorithm resolution, parsing behavior, and end-to-end token rejection. ## Changes **OIDC JWT Algorithm Confusion Fix** | Layer / File(s) | Summary | |---|---| | **Safe algorithm allowlist and resolver function**
`api/apps/auth/oidc.py` | Defines module-level constants for safe asymmetric JWT algorithms (`RS256`, `ES256`, `PS256`, etc.) and a resolver function that validates provider-advertised algorithms against the allowlist, falling back to `RS256` when metadata is absent or unsafe. | | **OIDCClient initialization with pinned algorithms**
`api/apps/auth/oidc.py` | Updates `OIDCClient.__init__` to compute and store `self.id_token_signing_algs` from OIDC discovery metadata using the resolver function; includes minor whitespace cleanup. | | **ID token parsing with pinned algorithms**
`api/apps/auth/oidc.py` | Reworks `parse_id_token` to pass `self.id_token_signing_algs` to `jwt.decode` instead of trusting the unverified JWT header, preventing algorithm-confusion attacks while continuing to use JWKS/`kid` to obtain the signing key. | | **Test harness updates for algorithm pinning**
`test/testcases/test_web_api/test_auth_app/test_oidc_client_unit.py` | Expands `_metadata` and `_make_client` helpers to accept optional `signing_algs` for injecting discovery metadata into tests; removes obsolete `jwt.get_unverified_header` monkeypatch. | | **Algorithm resolution unit tests**
`test/testcases/test_web_api/test_auth_app/test_oidc_client_unit.py` | Validates resolver logic: RS256 default when metadata absent, safe-allowlist intersection when present, fallback when only unsafe algorithms advertised, and robust handling of malformed/non-string entries and non-list metadata. | | **Parse ID token behavior tests**
`test/testcases/test_web_api/test_auth_app/test_oidc_client_unit.py` | Verifies `parse_id_token` forwards pinned algorithm allowlist to `jwt.decode` and does not consult `jwt.get_unverified_header`; includes sabotage test detecting header-based algorithm selection. | | **End-to-end token rejection tests**
`test/testcases/test_web_api/test_auth_app/test_oidc_client_unit.py` | End-to-end validation using real PyJWT encoding that `parse_id_token` rejects `alg: "none"` tokens and HS256-signed tokens when the pinned allowlist is asymmetric. | ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~45 minutes ## Poem > 🐰 *In OIDC realms where tokens fly,* > *We lock the algorithms high,* > *No header tricks shall pass us by—* > *RS256 keeps safe our sky!* > *With tests so thorough, none get through,* ✨
